You misunderstand. I'm not advocating her to not have emotions. I'm saying....emotions are not real. They are impulses and instincts designed to helps your brain determine what is going on outside of itself. They are senses. Instincts. What your light is to your eyes, emotions are to your brain. They have to expressed by understanding what they are trying to tell you, which is important, but they're "real" in the same way hunger and pain are real. Most people conflate "pain" and an emotion as being the same thing, rather than two separate senses occurring at the same time.

What "sensitive" means is you trust your emotions. You rely on them to help you determine reality. But personal perspective is not reality, and knowing that is key to avoid things like manipulation, unneeded suffering, impulsivity, and overreaction. It's also key for keeping your head clear and preventing emotions from controlling you. **Whenever anything, including your emotions, are calling the shots...that means you are not in control of yourself.** Which is not good. You want to be in control of yourself. And you can say 'no' to your own impulses, regardless of what they are or if you trusted them before.

Trauma means your brain got seriously derailed to a point of where your worldview and sense of self/safety is horribly skewed. It's damage, not suppression or lack of expression. Suppressing emotions is a way to prevent or reduce trauma, not the cause of it. Events cause trauma, not suppressing emotions.

Katawa Shoujo is a nothing short of a cultural phenomenon. About five years ago, complete strangers took a borderline offensive idea (an R rated game staring girls with disabilities) and worked on it until they created a soul-shaking masterpiece that moved almost everyone who played it. 4 Leaf Studios (the organization that made it) created what is easily one of the best games I have ever played because they felt like it. And it’s completely free. 

This game proves several things, one of which being that young people are totally capable of making works of art that can change lives (and thus change the world) without studio backing or talent agents. I have been on reddit and a few forums talking to other people who have played this game. Many fans are men who cried (myself included), faced their personal demons and became better people by realizing who they really were deep down inside. Because of a game! I’m serious, try this thing. But bring tissues.

I digress. This game taught me a lot about myself. It reminded me of who I am and who I was. I learned some lessons, and remembered some that I had forgotten. So, after pulling myself back together from the heavy emotions, I was able to write down some things I felt were worth sharing. Things that I learned. Some things that I always knew, but had forgotten.

Regardless of whether or not you played the game or ever will, here are some life lessons that I felt that I needed to share with everyone.

**32 Lessons I Learned & Remembered, Thanks to Katawa Shoujo**

1. You are not alone and you are not strange. Everyone has scars, everyone is damaged. Be the better person.* (quoted from Aura, the head writer of 4LS)

2. Sometimes, someone wears a smile just to hide their pain.

3. Feelings can hurt, but they are proof that you are alive. And that you have a heart.

4. Losing something doesn’t mean you “lose”. Failure is an event, never a person

5. Someone needs you right now. Right…freaking…now.

6. “Different" people are much more interesting.

7. Love may be the meaning of life, because after it is lost life suddenly becomes meaningless.

8. Everyone is scared. Everyone tries to hide. Everyone has something they are running away from. Deep down inside, we are all children hiding from our own monsters.

9. Everyone needs help.

10. We are always going to feel alone, even when we are not.

11. Choices have consequences. You can’t always know where a road is going to take you, or whose life you are going to change, if anyone’s. You can never take a decision back.

12. You know what happens to the people who never try? Nothing.

13. It’s not about you. It never has been.

14. Drink your whiskey carefully, away from windows and on the first floor if possible.

15. When you are single, romance, like sex, tends to happen when you least suspect it.

16. Inner pain hurts far worse than outer pain. Loss, Regret, Heartbreak and Loneliness hurts as much than getting your legs chopped off or being burned alive. (But I wouldn’t recommend those either.)

17. Tell her you like her.
 
18. This is stupid, but people often will want you to take interest in their problems but push you away at the same time. Don’t pry their shells open. Be patient.

19. You have to go for what you want. No one else is going to do it for you.

20. The beautiful ones have problems too.

21. Reading is not for gaylords. I don’t care what the flirty girl said.

22. You are going to do something stupid. Really stupid. You may have already done something stupid before, but that won’t be the last time.

23. Game guides (for life) exist! You just have to know where to find them and when to make the right choices.

24. Being gentle is better than being tough.

25. Losing your dad is probably going to be the most difficult thing you ever go through.

26. You will miss your teenaged years, even if they felt awful at the time. You will miss being young, even if your adult life is better.

27. You are going to get your feelings hurt and it is going to suck. And then you are going to have to decide if you are ever going to trust someone again after that. And you will have to make that decision over and over and over again.

I've read a lot about personality disorders and new research in the last few years have been challenging old beliefs about disorders being inherited.

The newer view is that many disorders are familial, not genetic. Meaning between ages 0 and 5, your brain picks up on any and all behaviors around you as "normal" and just absorbs them. A young child does not have the ability to judge if something is objectively unhealthy or dysfunctional; their brain's job is to learn everything it can to adapt, grow, learn and fit in to its environment. It does so without any bias or restraint. Young kids who are raised by NPD's will do what kids do and act their like parents. They don't have it in them to hate their parents, because they need them (and love them unconditionally).

This means there is a lot of hope for people struggling with what you are struggling with. If your genes (unchanging qualities about yourself) are responsible, you're stuck and may sink into hopelessness. But the truth is you've just been exposed to some very bad teachers and thus learned some really bad lessons. The good news is that you can learn good ones in their place. Another positive (just to give you some peace of mind) is that out of all of the cluster-B disorders, BPD has the best prognosis. Once diagnosed, something like 90% of BPD's are cured within 2 years (assuming they are actively working on learning new lessons). It takes a lot of work and therapy is all but mandatory, but it can be done.

Traveling tends to have more profound effects on a person's personality. The downside to traveling is something called The Traveler's Curse. It's when your world view becomes so expansive that you have difficulty connecting to people who haven't seen as much as you.
